title: AI-Driven Hip Exoskeleton Control for Diverse Users and Walking Tasks
official: AI-Driven Hip Exoskeleton Control Framework That Rapidly Generalizes to a Broad Range of Users and Real-World Locomotor Tasks
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the feasibility of a prototype artificial intelligence (AI)-based controller for a lightweight hip exoskeleton across a broad range of users, including healthy younger adults (18-39 years) and older adults (65 years and older). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can the AI-based controller accurately estimate gait phase in real time across younger and older adults?
* How does hip exoskeleton assistance change walking energy cost, mechanics, and muscle activity?

Researchers will compare walking with powered hip exoskeleton assistance to walking without the exoskeleton and walking while wearing the exoskeleton with no assistance (zero torque).

Participants will:

* Complete a short screening and frailty assessment
* Walk on a treadmill under different conditions with and without the hip exoskeleton during 2 to 5 lab visits
* Wear motion capture markers, muscle activity (EMG) sensors, and a mask that measures breathing to estimate energy use
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 to 39 years (younger adult group) or 65 years and older (older adult group)
* Willing and able to provide informed consent
* Able to walk independently without assistance
* No known cardiovascular, metabolic, or renal disease, and no signs or symptoms suggestive of such disease
* Cleared for light- to moderate-intensity exercise without the need for medical clearance under American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM) preparticipation screening guidelines

Exclusion Criteria:

* Age 40 to 64 years
* Leg surgery within the past 5 years
* Orthopedic disability that could impair movement or limit participation in the exercise protocol
* Neurologic disorder that may affect neuromuscular function or gait (e.g., stroke, Parkinson's disease, peripheral neuropathy, traumatic brain injury)
* Known metabolic or cardiovascular disease (hypertension alone is not exclusionary), or requiring medical clearance under ACSM guidelines without having obtained it
* Metal implants in the lower extremities, cardiac pacemaker, or other implanted electronic device
* Pregnancy
* History of seizure disorder or fainting (syncope)
